highlights.title: Virginia governor creates an AI task force and moves to restrain data centers
highlights.summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger (D) ordered the state government to take steps that could empower local communities to have a larger say in data center development and slow down approvals in a state that is already home to the data center capital of the world.
body: Gov. Abigail Spanberger (D) signed an executive order addressing data canters and AI risks.

Executive Order 22 bans executive branch officials from signing non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) for data center projects, requires expedited noise regulations, and a review of backup-generation operations used by data centers, among other requirements. The order also establishes an AI task force responsible for evaluating how the state government can address risks to Virginians like workforce displacement and data privacy issues, and determining how existing law can be applied to AI harms.

The order represents the latest signal that states are taking data center and AI policy into their own hands as Congress and President Donald Trump have been slow or resistant to sweeping changes. Also on Friday, California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) issued an executive order convening experts to tackle AI safety issues, and earlier, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott (R) have both taken executive action to rein in rapid data center development.

highlights.title: York Valkyrie win at Leeds to book Women's Super League Grand Final vs Wigan
highlights.summary: York Valkyrie are through to the 2026 Women's Super League Grand Final against Wigan Warriors following a superb 12-0 semi-final away victory over Leeds Rhinos.
body: York will now face defending champions Wigan in the Grand Final at the Brick Community Stadium on Sunday September 27 (5.30pm kick-off), live on Sky Sports.

York, who were beaten 38-16 by Leeds on August 8, and 44-0 by Wigan a week later on August 15, have totally turned fortunes around since, defeating Leeds at home, St Helens away and Wigan at home before sealing semi-final success.

The opening 21 minutes proved scoreless at Headingley in a tight contest, before York's Liv Wood twisted, turned and wrestled over to ground the ball for a try in the 22nd minute. Tara Jane Stanley converted for the full haul.

As the first half drew to a close and with Leeds camped on the York try-line on the verge of a try, a grubber-kick on the last by Leeds' Ruby Walker proved a poor one and allowed Stanley to gather and run clear.

highlights.title: Gavin Newsom is pushing for an AI kill switch
highlights.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) is positioning the state to take the lead on AI oversight, including the potential to mandate a "kill switch" for frontier models, with a new executive order issued Friday.
body: With Congress unlikely to act before the midterms, California is angling to take the lead.

There’s been a flurry of bill discussions in Congress in the wake of former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon’s post warning of a more than 10 percent chance that AI “could kill all humans” within a decade. But there’s little hope in Washington that a bill of substance could pass anytime soon given that the House is on recess until November, and the impending midterm elections make major legislation movement in the Senate similarly unlikely. At the same time, President Donald Trump has insisted, “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND ​SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!”

highlights.title: Spot the conversation hogger – and do something about it | Letter
highlights.summary: Penelope Mavor suggests that listening is not a passive act, so you could interrupt the flow. These conversational hoggers … don’t they know we were born with two ears and one mouth for a reason?
body: It is an interesting reflection to see which of the five hoggers more frequently turn up in our own lives. As a people pleaser and introvert, I have a track record of meeting many monologuists. I pretend to listen, but secretly resent them and their audacity. I just want them to ask about me.

I have learned that although interruption can feel violent, sometimes it is a courageous act. When the speaker has just lost connection with the audience and themselves, we have to bring them back. That is what I loved most about the article – it reminded us that we do have options. We can start noticing how we turn up. How am I listening and speaking? What is my responsibility here?
A great listener can help to transform the conversation – listening is not a passive act. And in talking, am I actually being interesting? Am I talking as if being listened to?

Anand jumping ship to Disney comes as a bit of a surprise considering how this time last year, the company was sending Character.AI cease-and-desist letters due to the startup’s tools infringing on copyrighted IP. But Anand’s hiring could be a sign of how Disney wants to move forward with AI now that its partnership with OpenAI has fallen apart.

highlights.summary: Brydon Carse will not face any charges after Derbyshire Police closed their investigation into an alleged assault following an incident involving the England cricketer at a nightclub in Derby.
body: Last month, Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby and missed the second and third Tests of England's series against Pakistan.

The 31-year-old was celebrating with Durham players after their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship and was also seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background.
In a statement, Derbyshire Police said: "An investigation into reports of an assault in Derby city centre has been closed.

"Officers attended Molly Malones in the Wardwick, Derby, in the early hours of Sunday 23 August. A man was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and was then de-arrested after his details were taken by officers."

highlights.title: What Hollywood thinks about existential AI warnings
highlights.summary: As the tech sector sounds alarms about AI's potential to destroy humanity, entertainment labor groups are urging the public to stay focused on what's already happening.
body: The studios have been silent, but Hollywood’s biggest labor unions aren’t buying the AI apocalypse narrative.

The AI tools used in entertainment production differ from the AI systems that have sparked a recent round of whistleblowing and apocalyptic declarations. They do not seem to be as existentially dangerous as the AI systems that drove former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon to quit his job and prompted Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger to insist that the technology could “kill all humans” at some point “within the next decade.”

When I recently spoke with the Screen Actors Guild – American Federation of Television and Radio Artists’ (SAG-AFTRA) chief negotiator Duncan Crabtree Ireland, he told me that the union recognized early on how AI could impact its members’ livelihoods. Most people might not have been familiar with the idea of studios completely replacing human actors with digital replicas, but SAG-AFTRA understood that it had an opportunity to shape public opinion about AI in Hollywood by “ speaking out about it at the earliest possible point we could.”

highlights.title: New Cat Species Discovered in Bolivia After Being Mistaken for a Kitten
highlights.summary: A new breed of cat has been discovered for the first time in 100 years. Citing the journal Current Biology, NBC News reports that a new wild cat species dubbed leopardus tilcayo (or the tilcayo tiger cat) was discovered in the Bolivian Yungas.
body: The tilcayo tiger cat is smaller than the average house cat, has rounded ears, a slender build, and is spotted.

Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, the co-author of Current Biology’s study, came upon the cat while volunteering for a wildlife rehabilitation center in Bolivia and thought it looked just different enough to warrant further investigation.

“The cat had been brought in by a man living in a community in the forest near La Paz who had mistaken the cat for a domestic kitten, according to details recorded by the sanctuary,” NBC reports. “He had fed the animal noodles, rice and eggs, only to realize it was wild and that he could not take care of it. So he brought it to the sanctuary.”
It was originally believed to have been a known species of wild cat, but Nogales-Ascarrunz conducted genetic testing that ultimately determined this was its own distinct cat species.

highlights.title: Gerrit Graham, Actor in ‘Phantom of the Paradise,’ Screenwriter and Grateful Dead Collaborator, Dies at 77
highlights.summary: Gerrit Graham, an actor, screenwriter and songwriter who co-wrote a song for The Grateful Dead, died on Tuesday in Rhinebeck, N.Y. He was 77. He suffered from lung disease, among other ailments.
body: As a screenwriter, Graham worked on projects including “The Little Mermaid,” “Oliver & Company” and episodes of “The Twilight Zone.” He co-wrote the Disney adaptation of “Prince and The Pauper” alongside his brother, Chris Hubbell. Also a songwriter and lyricist, Graham most notably collaborated with Bob Weir of The Grateful Dead. They co-wrote “Victim or The Crime,” which was recorded by the band for their “Built To Last” album and later by Weir and Rob Wasserman on their 1998 “Live” album.

Graham was born in New York City to parents John and Janet, and the family went on to live in Missouri and Michigan before settling in Chicago. In 1982, he married his wife, Deborah, with whom he had two children. He previously served on the Burger Hill Preservation Society while living in Rhinebeck, N.Y., for the last 30 years of his life after caring for his mother in California.
Graham is survived by his brother, Sam; his sons, Jack and Henry, and their wives, Talia and Joelle; and his four grandchildren, Nolan, Micah, Vera and Joey.

highlights.title: FCC lets Paramount sell 49.5% equity stake to Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar
highlights.summary: The Federal Communications Commission yesterday approved Paramount Skydance's plan to sell large equity stakes to the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Qatar.
body: Under US law, companies with licenses to run broadcast stations need FCC approval to have direct or indirect foreign ownership exceeding 25 percent of the company’s stock. Paramount says its indirect foreign ownership will reach 49.5 percent after it receives investments from the sovereign wealth funds and filed a petition asking the FCC to waive the foreign ownership limit.

Paramount, the owner of CBS, holds FCC licenses for the 28 local CBS stations that it owns and operates. Paramount is buying Warner Bros. Discovery in a $111 billion deal that is being partially financed with foreign investment but hasn’t completed the acquisition because US states filed a lawsuit that aims to block the merger. Trump’s Department of Justice approved the merger.

The FCC is letting Paramount sell indirect ownership stakes to “some of the most repressive governments in the world,” FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez, the only Democrat on the commission, said yesterday. “An investment this large in one of America’s biggest media companies doesn’t just buy equity, it secures influence over what gets said and what gets made.”

highlights.title: A new chapter for MIT Reads
highlights.summary: As it marks its 10-year anniversary, MIT Reads is being reimagined for the age of artificial intelligence. Recognizing the need to foster social connection and a sense of our shared humanity, the popular MIT Libraries’ program will turn its focus to fiction and memoir, and to the particular power…
body: “At MIT, we spend a great deal of time on imagining and building for the future. Reading fiction prompts us to think about how what we build might change us,” says MIT Libraries Director Chris Bourg. “Reading together also gives us the increasingly rare opportunity for both individual reflection and shared connection.”

MIT Reads is also evolving with MIT as it explores AI’s influence on the education landscape and the social fabric of the Institute. The value of collective reading, reflection, and discussion has never been more relevant.

A recently released report from MIT’s Ad Hoc Committee on AI Use in Teaching, Learning, and Research Training urges strengthening social connection and personal well-being, citing MIT Reads as a way to “engage many more people across campus in conversation about shared norms and why community matters.”

Launched in 2016, MIT Reads was designed to foster empathy, understanding, and belonging within the campus community. Each selected book is accompanied by programming such as talks by the featured author, panel discussions, and small-group conversations facilitated by library staff.

highlights.summary: “NAZA,” the acclaimed and controversial documentary about killings in Gaza, has set a distribution rollout for U.S. theaters starting Sept. 30 via an innovative plan that forgoes selling the film to a studio or independent distributor.
body: It’s looking like a busy fall for theatrical releases of documentaries: buzzy nonfiction titles set for October openings include Alex Gibney’s “Musk” on Oct. 9 and Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Elizabeth Holmes doc “You Can See Everything” on Oct. 16.

Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the two Israeli directors of the Oscar-winning documentary “No Other Land,” “NAZA” won a special jury prize at the recent Venice Film Festival. Its North American premiere is at The New York Film Festival on Sept. 26.
“No Other Land” was released in the U.S. through Cinetic with bookings by Michael Tuckman Media rather than using a traditional distributor.

Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, “NAZA” reveals in detail the systems behind “Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to the synopsis. NAZA is the military acronym used by Israeli intelligence to describe the number of civilians it expects will be killed in an airstrike.

highlights.title: Marks and Spencer’s first LFW catwalk gamble pays off with compelling looks at affordable prices
highlights.summary: Retailer’s message is ‘fashion with a small f’ as it picks up on trends and brings styles for everyone to debut runway show. Joan Collins declared the coats “very chic”, and has her eye on a graceful ivory evening dress with caped shoulders.
body: The show, held at the Design Museum for 310 guests including Ian Wright and Jamie Carragher, was a gamble on both sides. Would snobby fashionistas be traumatised by elasticated waistbands and practical rainwear? Would M&S customers be alienated by a world of £2,000 handbags and shoes you can’t walk in?

The style message was “fashion with a small f, not a capital F”, said the M&S womenswear director, Maddy Evans. The look was new enough to be compelling (sharp kilts instead of flouncy tiered skirts, low-rise slouchy denim replacing mom jeans), but pitched at a before-the-watershed comfort level. A judicious amount of catwalk theatre was added with some sauce (a very short skirt, the odd semi-visible nipple) and a little zeitgeisty styling (faux fur stoles, Charli xcx-adjacent sunglasses).

The real stunner is the price. All the clothes in this collection went on sale as the show began on Friday, with half of the pieces under £50. The most expensive, a leather coat, will retail for £450. The message – that catwalk style is for everyone – is a win for London fashion week, which has struggled to feel relevant to real lives as designer prices have soared during a cost of living crisis.

highlights.title: Finding the cells that put our brain to sleep
highlights.summary: For a long time, sleep research has treated the cerebral cortex as a passive follower reacting to signals from the deep brain. “Usually, sleep is associated with being controlled by subcortical regions,” said Geoffrey Terral, a neuroscientist at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine in New York.
body: The cortex is where the slow rhythms of deep sleep can be seen, but researchers assumed the signals that triggered them originated elsewhere. In a recent Nature study, Terral and Renata Batista-Brito, who runs the lab, report a population of cortical cells that challenges that assumption.

These cortical cells make up only around one percent of the cortex’s inhibitory neurons, and switching them on in a mouse puts the animal to sleep. “What our work shows is that the cortex can not only see this rhythm but also initiate it by itself, and this is sufficient to promote sleep,” Terral said.

The cells are called Sst-Chodl neurons, after two genes that are active in them. Long-range inhibitory neurons marked by the activity of these genes have been known for some time, based on studies in monkeys, but researchers couldn’t figure out how to manipulate them using these genes. Aiming at either one of these genes captures a huge, heterogeneous family of different neurons. “A single gene is not able to target these cells,” Batista-Brito said.

Rounds has been the beneficiary this cycle of around $600,000 in spending by outside groups, with the vast majority of that figure coming from the super PAC Defend American Jobs, which receives funding from a super PAC financed by the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.

He has also received roughly $215,000 directly from the employees and super PACs affiliated with AI labs, most notably Anthropic, as well as a constellation of other tech companies including Google and Microsoft, according to FEC filings.

With fewer than 50 days until the midterm elections in November, recent polls show Rounds ahead of the independent candidate Brian Beng after the Democratic candidate Julian Beaudion dropped out last month.

highlights.title: Is there romance in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave?
highlights.summary: Romance in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave sounds like a reasonable idea considering the vast roster you can recruit. In the game, the relationship between characters is represented by their support level.
body: Since in the series' previous games, you had to go through many steps to unlock "romantic endings," you may want to know if there's romance in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave. Below, we explain everything you need to know about it.

Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave does not feature a romance system like Fire Emblem: Three Houses' romance system. However, it doesn't mean that the game's story doesn't portray characters as romantically interested in others or being straight-up flirtatious.

As you play the game and raise a character's support level, you can unlock up to three support conversations — rank C, B, and A scenes. In some of these dialogues, you might see characters demonstrating their affection for each other. For example, Esmeralda won't hide her love for Dietrich from the beginning of the game. Even during the main quest, specific characters will explicitly engage in romantic interactions.

Even so, you won't find a romance system where you can choose and watch your favorite characters in a romantic scene. The closest Fortune's Weave gets to Three Houses ' S-Rank romance is the paired ending with Eshmel, the protagonist, but the scenes we played didn't have romance in them.

highlights.title: If the AI Industry Followed Its Own Research, It Might Have Paused Already
highlights.summary: Anthropic’s CEO says that safety hinges on understanding how AI “thinks.” So far the evidence is disturbing.
body: In early 2025 I was interviewing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei when he explained why, despite the company’s repeated acknowledgments that AI could yield catastrophic results, people seemed largely unperturbed. “There is compelling evidence that the models can wreak havoc,” he said. But, he added, those dangers were still theoretical. Would it take a Pearl Harbor–like situation for the world to wake up to those dire possibilities? He sighed. “Basically, yeah,” he said.

As it turned out, all it took was a well-timed X post from one of Amodei’s junior employees to accelerate AI fears to the top of the global agenda. On September 8, Jacob Coxon publicly posted his resignation, charging that Anthropic and other frontier AI companies were “racing straight to self-improving intelligence and gambling with our lives.” Almost instantly a more senior Anthropic engineer confirmed that many within the company thought that their work had a 10 percent chance of wiping out humanity.

The Bezzy doll is a stuffed plushie made in a satirical collaboration between the New York–based creative studio Basura and Big Data, the musical project of producer Alan Wilkis, best known for the song “ Dangerous,” a 2013 collaboration with the band Joywave. The joint project, which is coming out the same day as a new Big Data single, is called Adopt a Data Center. The goal is to present people with a “cuddly introduction to life with a real data center.”

Data Centers are very un -vogue right now. Built out by all the big AI companies to power their increasingly power-hungry AI tools, data centers have spread across thousands of acres of land in the US. They have been heavily criticized for their energy consumption and expansion of gas power. They have also proven to be audibly annoying, stirring up complaints about noise pollution from those nearby.

highlights.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold recalled by England but with a warning from Thomas Tuchel
highlights.summary: Real Madrid player must help improve defensive solidity. Scott, Hall, Lewis-Skelly and Calvert-Lewin selected. Thomas Tuchel has told Trent ­Alexander-Arnold he must bring defensive solidity to the England squad after giving him a surprise recall for the upcoming Nations League matches.
body: The head coach has selected the Real Madrid right-back only once before – for the games against Andorra and Senegal in June last year. Tuchel made headlines when he did so by urging Alexander-Arnold to focus on the defensive side of his game or risk a slip that could undermine the team’s World Cup campaign.

Tuchel used him as a 64th-­minute substitute against Andorra and ­Alexander-Arnold was out of the ­picture by the time England went to North America for the tournament. He is now back, despite starting only three of Madrid’s seven matches this season and largely going under the radar with his performances. Tuchel’s message to him has not changed.
“He has to, it’s necessary,” Tuchel said when asked whether Alexander-Arnold offered enough defensively. “My conviction is that he will but he has no choice.”

Tuchel continues to see ­Alexander-Arnold, who is famed for the range of his passing, as a right-back rather than a midfielder. The head coach has previously said he has Tino ­Livramento and Jarell ­Quansah ahead of Alexander-Arnold in the right-back pecking order. He has named both of them in the squad for the games against Spain (home), Czechia (home and away) and ­Croatia (away).

highlights.title: Wondering About Wool? These 5 Films Explain Fashion’s Relationship With the Fiber
highlights.summary: From farms to fashion weeks, these documentaries unpack the ethics surrounding wool production, one of fashion’s favorite natural fibers.
body: Since the Spring/Summer 2027 shows kicked off last Thursday, Peta protestors have crashed the runway twice. At Cos in New York and H&M in London, animal rights activists interrupted with demonstrations, holding banners saying, “Wool is bloody cruel” and “Sheep beaten and bloodied for wool, don’t buy it”. While Peta protests at fashion week are nothing new, many were perplexed by the idea that wool should be removed from the supply chain. After all, it is a natural fiber that humans have worn for centuries and — unlike fur — does not necessarily involve the death of an animal.

As material literacy continues to ramp up and consumers seek natural alternatives to polyester-based fabrics, wool may seem like a lasting, sustainable alternative. It has many helpful properties, including regulating body temperature, moisture, and odor. However, some experts take issue with the ethics surrounding its production, which can often entail cruel practices like mulesing.
